items.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I know I’m going to do some more work with Michael Moore. We’ll always work together a little bit.

ctx.x: Right. You’ve got it covered. What’s in the near future for you?

I’m hoping what’s in the near future is more of solo concerts and another solo CD. And I know I’m going to do some more work with Michael Moore. We’ll always work together a little bit. And some more festivals I hope. I think I’m playing at a festival in Poland next year. And I’m going to North Carolina and do some concerts there coming up. And doing a thing in Ohio, a tribute to Jobim playing a whole evening of his music, which is one of my other CDs that actually as voted one of the top ten CDs in Brazil. Just…
All right. Well it’s been great talking with you.

items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: my work with Gene Bertoncini... kept you two together for so many years... he gets jobs... featuring the bass in a very nice way

ctx.x: You must have got significant classical training in the conservatory? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

I did. I didn’t stay in the conservatory that long, but when I first started playing the bass I was thumping around on it, and thinking I was getting pretty good. My father brought home a bow, and he said, “Here, try it with this.” And it was so depressing when he did it. I didn’t touch the bass for about two weeks, and I really thought, do I really want to do this? And he said, “Well if you’re going to play the thing, you ought to learn how to play it right.” And I started with the principal bassist in the…
What is it about his playing that’s kept you two together for so many years?
